qs.q: What physical examination finding is typically observed in a child with spasticity affecting the ankle and gastrocnemius muscles?
o: Flaccid drop foot with absent deep reflexes
Equinovarus deformity and walking on tiptoe
Fixed hyperextension of the knee joint
qs.e: Increased tone in the antigravity gastrocnemius muscles causes an equinovarus deformity and often causes the child to walk on tiptoe. Flaccid drop foot with absent reflexes describes a hypotonic or lower motor neuron pattern rather than spasticity.

qs.q: A 60-year-old patient presents with an inability to plantarflex the ankle following a deep laceration behind the knee. Which nerve supplies the gastrocnemius muscle?
qs.e: Gastrocnemius is supplied by the tibial nerve, which innervates the posterior compartment of the leg. The common fibular nerve supplies the lateral and anterior compartments.
qs.s: Limb Anatomy Revision — Lower & Upper Limb: MCQs

qs.q: What is the primary nerve supply to the gastrocnemius muscle which forms part of the calcaneal tendon?
qs.e: The gastrocnemius muscle is supplied by the tibial nerve. The common fibular nerve supplies the lateral and anterior compartments of the leg.
qs.s: Limb Anatomy Revision — Lower & Upper Limb: MCQs
